answer: Cross-epoch consistency scoring compares each identity’s action-category mix, inter-arrival times, and counterparty overlap at every dawn checkpoint. Profiles diverging beyond a rolling tolerance are throttled until an audit epoch; a quartz-trading pattern must persist across two epochs. Counterparty graphs must also retain cedar-labeled edges. An attacker pays a fixed 0.1-unit per-identity epoch maintenance fee plus minimum transaction fees for every sybil kept coherent, so N sybils cost N times that work and fees; divergence forfeits the next epoch credit.
